_: THE WORKED-EXAMPLE GRAMMAR. FOUR FROZEN AXES. The author chooses the instructional structure. The renderer chooses ONLY the prescribed responsive state and the media subdesign belonging to that structure. Nothing else is inferred, ever. This is a non-shipping reference atlas; lesson-studio.html is frozen.
theOneRule: THE AUTHOR CHOOSES THE INSTRUCTIONAL STRUCTURE. THE RENDERER CHOOSES ONLY THE PRESCRIBED RESPONSIVE STATE AND MEDIA SUBDESIGN BELONGING TO THAT STRUCTURE.
whatNeverDecidesAnything: how tall the page turned out
— and the renderer never invents a tab, never moves content between tabs, and never treats a tall screen as a failure

composition.question: What is visible together, and where?

collection.question: If there are several related things, which are visible at once?

scroll.question: Which surface is allowed to move?

mediaGeometry.question: Which approved subdesign does the media shape permit?

axes._state: The responsive state is not a fifth axis. It is the prescribed wide/narrow arrangement OF a composition, from the surface width alone, and it can never select a different composition.

compositions._: The spatial relationship of currently visible content. Rigid horizontally, fluid vertically. The author writes the base name; media geometry resolves the suffix where one exists.

single.flow.wide: one column at the flow measure: title · QUESTION · rule · WORKED SOLUTION · ANSWER

visual.down.wide: the figure across the measure, interpretation beneath
visual.down.narrow: the same arrangement at a smaller plane — no state change

comparison.sharedVisual.side.wide: CASE A │ CASE B, then FIGURE │ INTERPRETATION

comparison.sharedVisual.down.wide: CASE A │ CASE B, then the figure across the measure with its interpretation beneath

collections._: Several RELATED things, and which of them are visible at once. A collection is not a composition: it says how many are visible, not how one is arranged. Its child is any composition.

collection.repeat.means: These are several sibling items; show them all, one after another.
collection.repeat.use: when seeing the sequence together is the point

collection.tabs.means: These are several SIBLING ITEMS; select one.
collection.tabs.example: Worked examples — [ Negative ] [ Fraction ] [ Decimal ] — three different examples
collection.tabs.use: when showing every item at full length makes a page nobody reads to the end

views.tabs.means: This is ONE instructional object seen in multiple REPRESENTATIONS.
views.tabs.example: Solving x² = 16 — [ Workings ] [ Graph check ] — one object, two views
views.tabs.use: solve it one way, then inspect the same idea another way
views.tabs.note: visualCheck is NOT a composition and has no rendering logic of its own. It is views.tabs{ Workings → single.flow, Graph check → visual.side|.down }. The same is true of a future [ Method 1 ] [ Method 2 ], which is views.tabs{ single.flow, single.flow } — not a new template.

views.stepper.means: one object walked through ordered stages

whyTheTwoTabKindsAreDistinct: collection.tabs and views.tabs look alike and mean importantly different things — SIBLINGS versus REPRESENTATIONS OF ONE THING. The distinction is encoded (`data-tabs-kind`), not merely styled: the affordance is keyed on the kind, so a views.tabs reads as a view switch wherever it appears and a collection.tabs reads as an item selector wherever it appears, at any nesting depth. The build asserts that.

scroll._: Two separate contracts, because a long equation is not the same design decision as an independently scrolling workspace. One enum cannot describe both.

page.means: the document may get arbitrarily tall
page.rule: Virtually all Notes, Worked Examples, Videos and ordinary teaching pages. Never compressed to fit a viewport.

pane.means: an explicit template feature — one pane moves while another stays
pane.use: the Workbook shape: QUESTION SET (local scroll) │ WORKBOOK (persistent)
pane.rule: NOT available as a renderer trick for making ordinary lesson content shorter. Teaching prose never sits in one.

local-when-needed.means: indivisible material overflows inside its own region
local-when-needed.use: a long equation, a table of values, perhaps code
local-when-needed.rule: It never widens its region, shrinks the type, or changes the composition. The page itself never scrolls sideways.

mediaGeometry._: EXTREMELY DUMB ON PURPOSE. From the authored domain's aspect at equal unit scale. It answers exactly one question — which approved subdesign does this composition use — and it may never answer `maybe this should be a different composition`.
mediaGeometry.proof: comparison.sharedVisual with a balanced figure resolves .side; with a wide figure it resolves .down. BOTH REMAIN comparison.sharedVisual. That is exactly the level of automatic behaviour wanted — a subdesign change with no semantic composition change.

switchPoints._: A switch point is PRESCRIBED, never searched. Most are a constant belonging to the composition. One is derived — and derived only from the authored figure's own preferred width and one design-system constant. It never looks at the prose, the step count or the height.
switchPoints.why: A fixed number cannot serve a figure system whose planes are 386–717px wide. At a 834px tablet a fixed 720 leaves a 488px plane beside a 314px reading column — narrower than the atlas's own 520px case measure. The derived point stacks instead, which is the right design and is still prescribed.
switchPoints.visual.down: none — the arrangement is the same at every width; only the plane's box changes

assembly._: A realistic Mathematics page. Every line of it is authored; nothing here is a measurement.

jsonPrinciple._: THE JSON DESCRIBES INTENT, NOT LAYOUT ARITHMETIC.
jsonPrinciple.test: The first set says what the lesson IS. The second tells CSS how to improvise. The build refuses the second: no authored file may carry a layout-arithmetic key.

later._: The assessment/workspace family gets its own rigid compositions rather than bending the teaching ones. Named here so nobody reaches for a teaching composition to build a workbook.

measures._: Design-system values. THEY NEVER APPEAR IN LESSON JSON. minInterpretation is the narrowest column the atlas will set reading prose in, and it is the one constant the derived switch point uses.

invariants.identity: Composition, collection and views are authored and never inferred. The build asserts the ordered list of compositions on a page, and the full tab structure, are identical at every width and in every tab state.
invariants.tabs: Tab structure — count, labels, panels, nesting, kind — is character-identical at every width. A tab is never created or removed by a viewport.
invariants.height: height:auto. The page scrolls. Page height is never an optimisation target and a tall page is not a failure.
invariants.measure: Every paragraph of prose renders within the flow measure. Unused page width is reading margin.
invariants.figures: A figure is sized from its own requirements. Surrounding prose never determines its width.
